title: Potential Medicare transition / benefits-cost discussion - April 2026 draft
summary: Draft HR planning notes for discussing Medicare options with employees in connection with a June 1, 2026 increase in RTEC health-plan costs. Because the source contains unfinished questions and missing information, it is evidence of a contemplated workflow, not an approved process.

claims.claim: In April 2026, HR was preparing information about Medicare options in anticipation of a June 1 increase in RTEC health-plan costs.
The draft contemplated explaining Part B and Part D income-related premiums and comparing Medigap and Medicare Advantage characteristics.

The document may represent an HR counseling/communication workflow for Medicare-eligible employees, but the final eligibility, employer-plan interaction, communication language and approval process are not established by this draft.

evidence.note: Contains explicit drafting questions and unfinished text.

trigger: Potential health-plan premium increase and identification of employees who may have Medicare options.
controls: Do not operationalize the draft without validating Medicare figures, legal/compliance implications and current RTEC benefit-plan rules.
unresolved_questions: Was a final version of this communication ever issued?
Which employees were intended to receive it and under what eligibility criteria?
What final June 2026 RTEC health-plan rates were approved?
Were the Medicare premium tables independently validated before employee use?
How does RTEC handle employer coverage, Medicare eligibility and coordination of benefits in current practice?
automation_candidates: Maintain a versioned benefits communication template sourced from approved plan-year figures.
Separate authoritative annual premium data from editable employee-communication language.

provenance.notes: Candidate only; source visibly contains unfinished drafting notes.
